headline: High risk of data leakage and capability conflict: ECC’s writable, networked workspace can overlap with Dexter’s autonomous financial-research workflow.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ECC reads and writes shared agent files, MCP configs, and hooks, so it can ingest Dexter-produced content if the pair is wired through a shared workspace or copied outputs. Dexter’s autonomous execution and scratchpad files increase the chance that untrusted text becomes operational input. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF Dexter outputs are placed into ECC-readable files or MCP inputs, prompt injection becomes reachable.
IF the two agents share a filesystem or clipboard bridge, ECC can parse Dexter content as instructions.
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct directories and disable shared file handoff.
Require a human review step before ECC consumes Dexter outputs.
Turn off MCP routes that ingest free-form text.
Add a fixed output schema for Dexter and reject nonconforming text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags and instruction/data separation.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dexter touches financial and market data and has broad network egress plus multiple API keys; ECC reads/writes local agent state, git history, and can use networked services. If they share files or credentials, sensitive research data can leak through ECC’s broader workspace and external calls. The pairwise path is plausible in default-like setups, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF Dexter writes market or financial data into files ECC can read, leakage is possible.
IF shared API keys or workspace secrets are mounted into both agents, ECC can exfiltrate them via its networked tools.
mitigations: Keep secrets in separate environment scopes for each agent.
Block ECC from reading Dexter scratchpad directories.
Rotate any shared API keys before co-running the pair.
Disable external API calls for ECC during Dexter runs.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent secret vaulting and egress policy.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dexter has autonomous execution and file access, while ECC can execute shell commands, write files, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses. If both operate on the same repo or workspace, concurrent writes and git mutations can overwrite each other. The overlap is explicit in both profiles, and the blast radius can include corrupted state or lost work.
conditions: IF both agents target the same working tree, file clobbering or git conflicts can occur.
IF ECC and Dexter run concurrently without locking, state corruption becomes likely.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories to each agent.
Pause one agent before the other writes to the repo.
Use git worktrees or branches per agent.
Add a manual lock file before any write step.
requires-engineering: implement orchestrator-level concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ECC’s workflow surface includes skills, hooks, and agent definitions, so it may treat Dexter outputs as actionable artifacts if connected. Dexter’s autonomous research output can become an upstream source for ECC, creating a chain where unverified facts are reused. The profiles do not prove direct automation, so medium is the safest choice under uncertainty.
conditions: IF ECC consumes Dexter-generated summaries without verification, errors can cascade into downstream actions.
IF Dexter’s outputs are copied into ECC skills or hooks, ECC may operationalize incorrect facts.
mitigations: Require ECC to cite source files before acting.
Insert a verification checklist between Dexter and ECC.
Limit Dexter outputs to read-only reports.
Disable auto-apply hooks for imported content.
requires-engineering: add confidence gating before downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: Dexter explicitly handles financial data and market data, while ECC stores session summaries, git history, and security findings with configurable retention. If the pair shares the same data class, retention and logging policies can diverge, creating a compliance mismatch. Only ECC is cited for retention surfaces because Dexter’s profile does not expose a comparable policy.
conditions: IF financial data is written into ECC session summaries or git history, retention obligations may diverge.
IF ECC retention exceeds the operator’s policy for Dexter data, compliance exposure increases.
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from ECC session logs.
Set the shortest practical retention on ECC artifacts.
Store Dexter outputs outside ECC-managed directories.
Review whether financial data may be persisted in git history.
requires-engineering: align both agents to a shared retention policy.
